inputs.root_cause: Per FF6-EVENT-000299's own exact_next_action, applied a fresh systematic pass over nrrd's remaining 18 obligations (which had not individually received this session's own 'check for hidden reuse' discipline as thoroughly as ora/xliff/ubl had). execution_steps: 1. Confirmed document.payload always holds the DECODED (post-decompression) form regardless of the file's original encoding (established earlier this session at FF6-EVENT-000291's own investigation) -- meaning payload itself represents the new encoding's own source data as-is and does not need to change when converting.

2. Traced writer.py's own _encode_payload(): binary = encode_binary(value.nrrd_type, value.sizes, value.array, ...) is computed FRESH from value.array (never from value.payload), then encode_encoding(binary, value.array, value.encoding, ...) applies whatever encoding value.header currently declares. This confirmed the writer is already fully self-sufficient for any encoding, given the right header value.

3. Verified directly with a standalone repro before writing any code: dataclasses.replace(document, header={**document.header, 'encoding': 'gzip'}) followed by dumps() and a reload correctly round-tripped the same decoded values. Repeated for ascii, hex, bzip2, raw -- all passed.

4. Implemented convert_encoding(document, target_encoding) -> tuple[NrrdDocument, EncodingConversionReport] in convert.py: validates target_encoding against SUPPORTED_ENCODINGS (raising NrrdWriteError with a clear message otherwise, matching writer.py's own validation message), returns a new document via dataclasses.replace() with only the header's encoding field changed, plus a report recording source/target encoding. Added EncodingConversionReport as a distinct dataclass from ConversionReport (dtype-shaped fields like overflow_policy/clipped_indices do not apply to a lossless encoding change), with is_lossless always True (documented why, not left as an unexplained bare constant).

5. Wrote 9 tests (test_obligation_encoding_conversion.py): every supported encoding round-trips correctly (parametrized); case-insensitive target name; refuses an unsupported encoding name; does not mutate the source document (dataclasses.replace() returns a new object); converting to the same encoding is a correct no-op.
6. Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full nrrd suite (631 passed, was 622), and the 6-format regression (3685 -> 3694 passed, +9, 0 failed).

7. Narrowed (not closed) SAL-NRRD-OBL-E2B0331E7D4F6AD8: encoding conversion is now cited as resolved in implemented_behavior; missing_behavior updated to name only attached/detached form conversion (a genuinely separate, larger file-splitting/joining feature) and dtype scaling as the remaining gaps, honestly distinguishing them from the now-resolved encoding-conversion clause.
